correctness.rationale: The full vertex-set definition permits top faces only of distributions (3,2) and (3,1,1). Every (3,1,1) top face has a distinct codimension-one face with a unique top coface, so integral cycle coefficients there vanish. The remaining (3,2) faces decompose by unordered block pair; their boundary rows are disjoint and each pair has the six-facet boundary matrix of a five-simplex. The integer kernel for one such boundary is Z times its alternating six-facet chain, with unit coefficients, and no five-simplices can bound it. This proves Z^{binom(r,2)} and primitivity for all r. Block swaps introduce the sign (-1)^9, yielding exterior-square equivariance. Inclusions preserve generators with an explicit new-pair complement. CHECKER.py recomputed top-face incidence, mod-two rank, signed generators and symmetry for r=2..8; these checks corroborate, rather than replace, the infinite integral proof.

value.rationale: The multi-facet generalization of the classical two-block tolerance sphere has a canonical and previously non-implied integral top-homology lattice supported on exact six-facet representatives. The proof supplies a stable inclusion law, a sharp integral cycle-support cutoff and the complete natural block/vertex permutation representation, not merely a numerical finite example. These identify the fate and symmetry of top-dimensional cycles under adding arbitrarily many new disconnected triangle blocks and complement known abstract Leray/collapsibility bounds.
